answer.value:
Hammurabi's Code:
Hammurabi's code based on the principle of "an eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth."
It ensured that the same harm was inflicted on the perpetrator as he was caused to the victim.
This code was formulated to protect Babylonian society, including women and slaves.

questions.text: Mention the historical significance of the Great Wall of China.
questions.text_as_printed: Mention the historical significance of the Great Wall of China. (A)

answer.value:
The Great Wall of China:
China originally consisted of many small states.
These were later unified into seven large states.
To protect the unified state, independent walls were built along the borders.
These walls were connected to prevent invasions from the north.
Construction of the Great Wall began in the 7th century BCE and Continued until the 16th century BCE.
Spanning 5,000 kilometers, it is one of the wonders of the world.

answer.value:
Shang Dynasty Military:
Shang kings spent considerable time in wars and invasions.
They gave significant importance to the military.

Archaeological findings include bronze knives, axes, bows, and arrows with metal tips used by them.
